encounters.cc: Worsening lower urinary tract symptoms after recent retention episode

lines: Worsening lower urinary tract symptoms after recent retention episode
The patient returns for urologic evaluation with chronic hypertension, diabetes, cognitive impairment, and recent medication-related cough.
He reports nocturia (3–4 times per night), weak urinary stream, urinary urgency, and difficulty initiating urination.
He has also experienced two episodes of painless gross hematuria and was hospitalized last month for acute urinary retention requiring catheterization.
Six months ago, he was started on tamsulosin, which helped initially, but symptoms have returned.
His medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
Digital rectal exam reveals a firm, symmetrically enlarged prostate.
A recent bladder ultrasound shows increased prostate volume and a post-void residual volume of 220 mL.

encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty walking and hand numbness over 6 months

lines: Progressive difficulty walking and hand numbness over 6 months
The patient with cognitive impairment returns.
He reports his legs feel stiff and he has tripped several times recently.
His past medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypercholesterolemia.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
On physical examination, you note decreased grip strength and atrophy of the intrinsic hand muscles.
Reflexes are diminished in the upper extremities but hyperreflexic in the lower extremities.
A positive Babinski sign is present bilaterally.
MRI of the cervical spine reveals multilevel degenerative changes with evidence of spinal canal narrowing at the C5-C6 level.

encounters.cc: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral leg swelling over 3 months

lines: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral leg swelling over 3 months

This 71-year-old male with history of hypertension, diabetes, prior lisinopril-induced cough, and cervical myelopathy presents with a 3-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower extremity edema.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
His medications include metformin, amlodipine, and atorvastatin.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute
He has jugular venous distension, crackles at the lung bases, and a 2+ pitting edema up to the shins.
The cardiac examination reveals a laterally displaced point of maximal impulse and a third heart sound (S3).
- Chest X-ray: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with cephalization of pulmonary vasculature

encounters.cc: Sudden severe chest pain radiating to left arm with nausea and diaphoresis

lines: Sudden severe chest pain radiating to left arm with nausea and diaphoresis

The patient is a 73-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and prior heart failure who presents to the emergency department with a 2-hour history of sudden-onset, severe chest pain radiating to his left arm, associated with nausea and diaphoresis.
He describes the pain as "pressure-like" and rates it 9 out of 10.
His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
On examination, his blood pressure is 160/90 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute.
His cardiac biomarkers are as follows:
An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF.

encounters.cc: Sudden left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking

lines: Sudden left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking

This 74-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, and a history of myocardial infarction and heart failure is brought to the emergency department by his wife after he developed sudden weakness on the left side of his body and difficulty speaking while eating breakfast.
His symptoms started approximately 2 hours ago, and he is given intravenous medication to improve neurologic recovery.
- Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) of inferior wall (diagnosed 2025-01-15)
He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia.
His medications include lisinopril, metformin, and atorvastatin.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.
On arrival, his blood pressure is 154/92 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.
Neurologic examination reveals left facial droop sparing the forehead, decreased strength in the left upper and lower extremities, and expressive aphasia.
Non-contrast CT scan of the head shows no hemorrhage.

encounters.cc: Sudden dizziness, nausea, and difficulty walking for 4 hours

lines: Sudden dizziness, nausea, and difficulty walking for 4 hours

This 75-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, asthma, and an ischemic stroke in 2026 is brought to the emergency department by his wife for a 4-hour history of sudden-onset dizziness, nausea, and difficulty walking.
He reports the room is spinning and has vomited twice since symptoms began.
- Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) of inferior wall (diagnosed 2025-01-15)
He has a 30-year history of hypertension and type II diabetes.
His medications are lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin, metformin, glyburide, and a daily multi-vitamin.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
On examination, he has horizontal nystagmus, worse with gaze to the right.
There also appears to be a mild Horner syndrome on the right.
There is right limb ataxia and dysmetria of the right upper and lower limbs on finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing.
Muscle strength is preserved, and there are no signs of weakness or sensory loss.
His speech is mildly slurred, and he veers to the right when attempting to walk.
